topic.title: Transfer of task-private utility to the strongest pair-rank-occupancy representation
topic.question: Under the frozen inputs and training protocol, does the committed task-private approach retain incremental utility on the newer pair-rank-occupancy source, exceeding both frozen source bests, especially validation four-task macro ROC-AUC 0.831886841754755, at justified parameter and measured compute cost?
topic.hypothesis: Nearest available work is the committed pair-rank and task-private summaries plus the unsuccessful exchange/rank contrasts; code and papers are unavailable, and external novelty is unverified. Inherit only the two committed approaches after implementation inspection in the next phase. The proposed difference is testing task-private utility on the newer representation rather than the older memory-joint entry. Task-specific information may remain useful, but shared ancestry, redundancy, task interference, capacity and seed variation are alternative explanations. Preserve both frozen source bests; source-replacement/factorial and matched-capacity controls, with measured training/inference costs, would distinguish compatibility from added capacity if budget permits. Failure to exceed the stronger source weakens this transfer hypothesis; improvement only over the weaker source is insufficient. One positive run supports provisional utility, not a mechanism; controlled attribution and repetition require reserved resources. Freeze selection and comparison suite before a single held-out assessment; withheld outcomes cannot guide further open research.
